# Results

**Generated by `audit.py --write-results`. Do not edit by hand.**

66 registered lower bounds on the kissing number tau(n), compared with their
recorded published baselines. Later superseding records are listed in README.md.

The 26 October continuation gives 197584 in 25D, 241742 in 31D, 610394 in 38D, 769180 in 39D and 1126314 in the newly registered dimension 40. All five independent exact replays passed. Fresh primary-source comparisons and the unavailable Cohn retrieval are documented in common/source_review_20261026.json. The 24 October 2026 checkpoint adds exact Coxeter-Todd constructions in dimensions 36 and 37, registers the supplied 2 919 743-point partial-family 43D certificate, and raises 45D to 7 655 056. All 41-46D integer angles and head dimensions replay; complete-family body populations inherit the documented identities and have not all been freshly enumerated. The 25 October continuation adds shared midpoint replacements with 200,918 points in 26D and 204,636 in 27D, adds 216,568 points in 29D and 224,280 in 30D, regains 38D with 605,346 and 39D with 768,924, and strengthens 73D and 76-96D. The norm-ten continuation gives 6,218,204,076 in 73D and exact finite-graph existence bounds in 77-79D. The checkpoint also includes the 205,232-point joint Leech lift in 28D, the 7 387-line P48 class family, code constructions in 61-68D and 95-96D, including the new signed-support 64-65D constructions, and Gamma72 nearest-coset lifts. The comparison column uses common/published.py's pinned published data; this integration is not a new comprehensive literature audit. The paper now reports the current records in its main table and preserves the earlier snapshot in its historical appendix. See [verification scope](verifications/improved/dim41-46-p48-heads/README.md).

## Status: what would have to change

A status describes THIS PROJECT'S MECHANISM in that dimension, not tau(n).  No matching upper
bound is known in any dimension here, so no value below is known to be optimal --
`exhausted` means the idea is finished, not the dimension.

| status | dims | what it means | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `classes` | 49-60 (12) | only a better class family helps; these all improve together | the strongest prefix of the old 1400-class family or the October 577-image family over a 7387-line base; larger base classes and different disjoint families remain open (dim49-63-p48-caps/verify_october.py) |
| `classes` | 87-94 (8) | only a better class family helps; these all improve together | the cap DIRECTIONS are at their ceiling -- the partition into zero-sum triples is perfect where one exists, and three is the most a class line can ever serve.  The class FAMILY is what moves, and it moved twice in one session (KNOWLEDGE 90, 91): the class size 2465 is a factor 11.2 over Caro-Wei against the Leech lattice's 11.3, so matching that would be a further 1% on every one of these 23 dimensions.  The AXIS layer was rebuilt on 2026-08-27 as a ROTATED COPY of the cap directions, which is a 60-degree code for free and only has to clear the 30-degree caps: at k = 23 it gives 93074 poles against the shell rule's 248, and it reaches tau(k) exactly at k = 3, k = 5, k = 6, k = 7, k = 8, k = 9, k = 10, k = 11, k = 14, k = 16.  What is left there is the handful a rotation loses to the caps, and, where the cap set has fewer than tau(k) vectors, the gap between the two -- 602 points in total, against a claim of 6.4e9, and 321 of them are the two the record configuration of R^k cannot be carried into (k = 12 is given in floating point by the data set, k = 13 differs from K_13 in Hasse invariant).  The class family is the only thing that moves this group (scripts/axis_rotate.py, scripts/axis_block.py, scripts/verify_poles.py) |
| `codes` | 39 (1) | larger input codes or different layer and section geometry can improve these explicit constructions | rationally deformed dense sign orbits and sparse root replacements; complete relative orbit enumeration; larger compatible families remain open (dim39-deformed-orbits/verify.py) |
| `codes` | 61-63, 66-68, 95-96 (8) | larger input codes or different layer and section geometry can improve these explicit constructions | explicit binary compression, central sections and enlarged support layers; no unrestricted optimality or construction ceiling is claimed (dim61-68-95-96-code-layers/verify.py) |
| `codes` | 64-65 (2) | larger input codes or different layer and section geometry can improve these explicit constructions | signed support augmentation with exact shared-check parity certificates; larger compatible support families and larger owner classes remain open (dim64-65-signed-parity/verify.py) |
| `cosets` | 36-37 (2) | larger phase codes, nearest subsets or improved compatible tail assignments remain open | exact Coxeter-Todd short shells and phase-orbit angles replay; 37D adds two latitude layers. Larger phase codes remain open (dim36-37-coxeter-todd/verify.py, phase/proof.txt) |

Larger coupled family changes, partial families and new body models remain open; finite search optima are not global ceilings. The partial-family 43D and coordinated-motion 45D certificates are installed (dim41-46-p48-heads/README.md, verify.py, POPULATIONS.txt) |
| `lp-exact` | 69-71 (3) | the programme solved to its EXACT optimum, for a Gram at the Hermite determinant floor; only a larger k helps | the k-point programme solved to its EXACT optimum by common/exact_vertex.py, which substitutes out the identifications and solves the dual vertex in rational arithmetic rather than rounding a float, so the value is the most this programme can certify: no basis, dual or solver setting moves it, and all sixteen determinant-256 presentations agree at k = 3.  The Gram determinant is at the Hermite floor, which is a theorem, and the tuple is exhibited in Gamma_72.  That the lowest determinant gives the best bound is measured across the k = 3 table, not proved.  So only a larger k could help, and k = 5 extrapolates below the floor (scripts/verify68.py, verify69.py, k4_gram_min_det.py, presentation_invariance.py) |

So the 20 `classes` dimensions all improve together when a better family of pairwise-disjoint
classes is found -- which is where compute pays -- and the other 46 need a new idea or a
refreshed table, not more search.

## Not claimed, and why

| dim(s) | why |
|---|---|
| 32-35 | older ERS/cross-section audit; no new construction registered here. `verifications/closed/dim32-44-ers-audit/` |
| 47 | already in the literature. 23 766 960 is Boyvalenkov-Cherkashin, Results Math. 80 (2025), Paper No. 3, equation (3) of the preprint arXiv:2312.05121. The historical 46D value 12 309 600 is Sun-Wang, arXiv:2607.20359, Table 3; the new 46D construction is larger. `verifications/recovered/dim46-47-p48-cross-sections/` |
| 48 | 52 416 000 is P_48 itself. |
| 72 | 6 218 175 600 is Gamma_72 itself. |
| 97 and above | **not evaluated here.** Monotonicity gives at least dimension 96's 13 289 406 656, and nothing in this repository claims anything there. The Edel-Rains-Sloane chain is the thing to evaluate, as it was at 96. |
| 9-17, 19 | every published record is checked MAXIMAL -- no sphere can be added to any of them, and the margin of each is recorded. `verifications/closed/dim09-19-record-maximality/` |
| 17, 19-21 | the Cohn-Li mechanism is at its exact ceiling: provably exhausted in 20 and 21, dimension 19 closed at exactly Ho's 11948, and dimension 17 at its two-slot value; the middle dimension of that range left this table for the improved tier (the bent-coset hexagon). `verifications/closed/dim17-23-cohn-li-mechanism/` |
| 17, 19-24 | one construction, not eight: every Leech minimal vector's part in the 8 coordinates of an octad has norm^2 0, 8, 16 or 32, the multiplicity is CONSTANT on each of those four position shells (4320, 512, 32, 1), and hence tau(Lambda_{16+k}) = 4320 + 513*N_2(L_k) + 32*N_4(L_k) for L = A1, A2, A3, D4, D5, E6, E7, E8.  The records add a flat layer, which is EXACTLY 2048 in 20 and 21 (Koenig on a regular bipartite Cayley graph) -- both are rebuilt there from the Golay code and checked pair by pair.  The one component not at a proved ceiling is the tier size, in [512, 533]. `verifications/closed/dim17-24-layer-identity/` |
| 22, 23 | Lambda_22 and Lambda_23 are maximal spherical codes, and Leech level sets cap at exactly 93150. `verifications/closed/dim22-23-maximal-cross-sections/` |
| 24 | 196560 is the Leech lattice, and it is optimal (Odlyzko-Sloane, Levenshtein). |

Dimensions 25 to 31 left this table on 2026-09-15, when dimension 28 became the last of them to be claimed. The cap model still reproduces Cohn's table *exactly* in 26, 28, 29, 30 and 31 --- that is what `verifications/improved/dim73-95-gamma72-caps/scripts/calibrate.py` checks --- and in each of those five a layer now beats the template that calibration validates.

**An exposure, at dimensions 93-95.** These three ARE claimed, above; this is about how much room they have. Every Edel-Rains-Sloane input is a construction, so its totals are LOWER bounds: one above Gamma_72 settles a dimension, one below it settles nothing. At 93-95 the chain reaches only 2.68e9, 2.68e9 and 4.83e9, which proves nothing by being small, so the package reports the threshold instead. Dimension 95 stands as long as A(95,23,23) < 341 303, against 65 536 from the best construction in hand, on the chain (95, 23, 4, 1). `verifications/closed/dim96-ers-takeover/`
